Giving Reasons: Because of, Due to, Owing to

You use reason clauses to express the reasons for an action, or why a situation is the way it is.
You use words like because of, due to, and owing to to introduce a noun phrase to give a reason for something.

Reason clauses are subordinate to the main clause. They state the reason why things are done, or what makes a situation the way it is.
You can use because of, due to or owing to to introduce a noun phrase that gives a reason for a situation.

Example:
She was injured because of an accident.
We have less money owing to / due to budget cuts.

Skimming a Text

Skimming and scanning are two very different strategies for reading texts quickly and for getting the information you need from them without wasting time.
Knowing when to use these skills will help with your reading abilities and comprehension skills.

Skimming:

Skimming refers to looking only for the general or main ideas in a text.
When you skim, your overall understanding is reduced because you don't read everything. You read only what is important to your purpose.
One technique for effective skimming is reading only the first line of each paragraph, since these are the topic sentences and will give you an idea of what the main idea of each paragraph is.
For example:

These extreme shifts in energy are the effects of jet lag.
Jet lag can affect each person differently.
There are several effective remedies for jet lag.
What's the very best way to avoid jet lag?
Scanning:

Scanning refers to looking for specific information in a text. Examples of scanning in daily life are: bus schedules, movie schedules, phone lists etc. When you use these kinds of texts, you are only looking for a specific detail (a number, a date, a name etc.).
Knowing the structure of the text you want to scan will help you do it quickly (alphabetical, numerical, categorical, chronological).
Try skimming and scanning the text for the general ideas and for specifics.

images.text: Seasoned travelers know all too well the feeling of being wide awake, suddenly, at 2:00 a.m., and then feeling dead tired at 2:00 p.m. These extreme shifts in energy are the effects of jet lag, which occurs due to changes in your body's circadian rhythms. Jet lag, known medically as desynchronosis, generally manifests itself as trouble falling asleep when traveling east, and trouble waking up when traveling west. Other symptoms can include fatigue, poor concentration, headaches, irritability and often indigestion.

Jet lag can affect each person differently; however, a good rule of thumb is that one day of recovery is required for each hour of time difference between the city of departure and the destination. That's means if you travel from Toronto to Frankfurt, you will need six days to fully recover, owing to the fact that Frankfurt is six hours ahead of Toronto. If you travel from Bogota to New Delhi, the adjustment period will be more like ten days. Los Angeles to Miami? Just three days.

There are several effective remedies for jet lag. The first step is avoiding bright light, especially in the morning. Due to the fact that it is produced in dim light, the hormone melatonin can also be taken as a supplement to help combat the effects of jet lag. Finally, there are special glasses that can be worn to provide extra light at specific intervals. Owing to the possibility of accidents caused by jet lag, most airline pilots and crew must complete a mandatory rest period before moving from one destination to another.

What's the very best way to avoid jet lag? Travelling north-south, of course! That's because of the fact that jet lag only affects those travelling east-west, across time zones. So next time you plan a trip from Cairo, think about flying south to Johannesburg, not east to Beijing.

contents.value: Seasoned travelers know all too well the feeling of being wide awake, suddenly, at 2:00 a.m., and then feeling dead tired at 2:00 p.m. These extreme shifts in energy are the effects of jet lag, which occurs due to changes to your body's circadian rhythms. Jet lag, known medically as desynchronosis, generally manifests itself as trouble falling asleep when traveling east, and trouble waking up when traveling west. Other symptoms can include fatigue, poor concentration, headaches, irritability and often indigestion.

When travelling alone for the first time, the teenagers' sensation of freedom could lead them to either feel ecstatic and have the time of their lives or become completely frightened and make wrong decisions. It is not only a new experience for these kids traveling and facing the world on their own but, also, for their parents who always knew and feared this moment would arrive. Whether they're going on a school trip or an actual trip all by themselves, these kids need to have been educated to behave themselves well without the constant supervision of any grown-up.
